tools.name: ds_read
tools.description: Read one or more addresses in a single call. Takes an ARRAY of paths: name everything you need at once rather than chaining calls, which is measurably cheaper and is the main reason this tool is batched. Reads a context document, a CRM record, a window of workbook rows, a public URL, or a skill. Use `fields` to project only what you need from wide records. Do not use this to find something whose address you do not know yet: that is ds_search. skill://<name> loads the procedure, quality bars and traps for one job, and is how you obey an instruction to load a skill before doing something; ds_search scope=skills lists which ones exist. An https:// path costs credits and leaves the workspace, so it requires a purpose; everything else is free.

fields.name: paths
fields.description: Array of addresses to read in one call. Schemes: context:// (document or folder/ trailing slash), record://<object>/<id>, workbook://<id>[/<column>], skill://<name>[/<file>], https://. Prefer one batched call over many single-path calls, up to 50 addresses per call; split into multiple calls beyond that.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Optional column projection for workbook:// addresses only: mapped to visible_column_ids on worksheet.viewport. Ignored for context://, record://, skill:// and https://. Maximum 50 field names.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: Optional page size for context:// folder browse and workbook:// viewport reads only. Ignored for single-document, record, skill and https paths.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: Required when any path is https:// (costs credits and leaves the workspace). One short sentence. Optional and unused for free in-workspace reads.

fields.name: max_credits
fields.description: Required when any path is https://: a positive credit ceiling for that fetch (research.urls_fetch has no fixed price, so the gateway cannot bound its cost without one). Applies to every https:// path in this call, batched or not. Ignored and unused for free in-workspace reads.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates paths and policy only. dry_run may perform real reads but cannot create an effect. live performs the requested read.

tools.name: ds_write
tools.description: Create a new context document or folder. Use this for durable knowledge the workspace should keep: what was learned about a customer, a positioning note, a playbook. Do not use it for a message, a post or a record field, which have their own tools. What you write is an ordinary file a human can open, edit and delete, so put it in a folder a person would have chosen and link it to what it relates to with [[links]]. Every claim you write carries where it came from and when. parent_path MUST be a context:// address (example "context://" for root, or "context://brain:workspace:<id>:folder:<uuid>"); never a filesystem path like "/". Discover folders with ds_search scope=context when you do not already have one. create_document also requires content and, once this workspace has a published document, related_paths (existing context://...document:<uuid> addresses). The first document in an otherwise empty workspace may omit related_paths; this is checked against the live workspace, not assumed from the call.

fields.name: parent_path
fields.description: REQUIRED. Parent folder as a context:// address ONLY (scheme + optional node_ref). Accepted form: "context://" for workspace root, or "context://" + an existing folder node_ref (example: "context://brain:workspace:<workspace_id>:folder:<uuid>"). Never a filesystem path ("/", "/sources", "/context/...", "/notes/..."). How to obtain a non-root folder: call ds_search with scope=context (or ds_read on a folder path ending in /) and use a returned context:// folder address. create_folder: root "context://" is valid. create_document: MUST be an existing non-root folder (not bare "context://"). register_source with brand_url: parent is unused; pass "context://" if you have no folder. Seeded workspaces often only have root and a few system folders; discover them rather than inventing paths.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Human-readable name for the document, folder, or source.

fields.name: content
fields.description: create_document: REQUIRED body of the new document. create_folder and register_source: omit.

fields.name: related_paths
fields.description: create_document: REQUIRED once this workspace has at least one published context:// document, so a new document links to what it relates to and stays reachable by search-then-walk instead of becoming an orphan. One or more existing published context:// document addresses in this workspace (form context://brain:workspace:<workspace_id>:document:<uuid>). Maximum 20 addresses per call. Obtain them from ds_search scope=context or a prior ds_read. The facade appends markdown links to them before create+publish. Omit ONLY when this would be the first document in an otherwise empty workspace (checked server-side against the live workspace, not taken on your word) or for create_folder and register_source. If the workspace already has a published document and you omit related_paths, the call is refused before anything is created.

fields.name: subject_user_id
fields.description: Optional subject owner for a private document or folder under a person root.

fields.name: source_kind
fields.description: register_source (non-website): one of uploaded_file | website | url_capture | crm_import | provider_payload. Omit when brand_url is set (website path).

fields.name: media_type
fields.description: register_source (non-website): MIME type of the uploaded object.

fields.name: byte_size
fields.description: register_source (non-website): size in bytes, max 26_214_400.

fields.name: content_object_id
fields.description: register_source (non-website): UUID of the already-uploaded content object.

fields.name: content_digest
fields.description: register_source (non-website): 64-char lowercase hex SHA-256 of the content bytes.

fields.name: brand_name
fields.description: register_source website path: brand display name. Defaults to title when omitted.

fields.name: brand_url
fields.description: register_source website path: when set, routes to website_source_register and does not need the uploaded-source fields. HTTP(S) URL.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: One user-facing sentence on what this call is trying to obtain. Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates the selected request and policy without reads, providers, credits, or effects. dry_run previews without effect; only honoured when the resolved capability declares dry_run_supported. Otherwise expect preview_unsupported and use live after confirming the intended change.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key for a deliberate retry of the same mutation. Omit for a first call; dispatch derives a stable key from the resolved request so a retry collapses onto its predecessor. Supply your own only when two deliberately identical mutations must both run.

fields.name: proposal
fields.description: Architect discovery only: the complete typed proposal produced by this successful live write. Its chat_session_id must match the server-bound tool session. The turn/job layer persists it and owns job/release identity.

tools.name: ds_edit
tools.description: Change part of an existing context document by replacing an exact string, or move, rename, archive and restore documents. Prefer editing over rewriting: a targeted replacement preserves everything a human wrote around it. Read the document immediately before editing it. Archive rather than delete unless the user explicitly asked for deletion or it is a privacy request.

fields.name: path
fields.description: context:// address of the document. Prefer the node_ref returned by ds_read, as context://brain:workspace:<ws>:document:<uuid>. Lifecycle actions (move/rename/archive/restore/delete) map this to document_id; replace and rebuild_links map it to node_ref.

fields.name: old_string
fields.description: replace: REQUIRED. Exact substring to replace; must occur exactly once in current_content.

fields.name: new_string
fields.description: replace: REQUIRED. Replacement text (may be empty to delete the matched span).

fields.name: current_content
fields.description: replace: REQUIRED. Full current body from a prior ds_read of path. The facade verifies old_string is unique here, then sends the substituted body; it does not re-read the document.

fields.name: publish
fields.description: replace only. Default true: compile to brain.context.save_and_publish (Architect principal may publish a workspace-private Context document directly). Set false to save a draft only (brain.context.save_draft).

fields.name: expected_revision_id
fields.description: replace: optional optimistic concurrency. Mapped to expected_published_revision_id when publish is true, else expected_revision_id. Null means unconditional overwrite of the current head.

fields.name: expected_document_revision
fields.description: move, rename, archive, restore, delete: REQUIRED integer. Use lifecycle.revision_counter from a prior ds_read of this document. Not used by replace or rebuild_links.

fields.name: revision_id
fields.description: rebuild_links: REQUIRED. Exact published revision id (UUID) to reparse [[links]] from.

fields.name: target_folder_path
fields.description: move: REQUIRED. context:// address of the destination folder.

fields.name: expected_folder_path
fields.description: move: REQUIRED. context:// address of the folder the document is currently in (optimistic concurrency on folder_id).

fields.name: title
fields.description: rename: REQUIRED. New document title. Not used by other actions.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: One user-facing sentence on what this call is trying to obtain. Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates the selected request and policy without reads, providers, credits, or effects. dry_run previews without effect; only honoured when the resolved capability declares dry_run_supported. Otherwise expect preview_unsupported and use live after confirming the intended change.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key for a deliberate retry of the same mutation. Omit for a first call; dispatch derives a stable key from the resolved request so a retry collapses onto its predecessor. Supply your own only when two deliberately identical mutations must both run.

tools.name: ds_search
tools.description: Find things whose address you do not know. Five scopes. `context` searches the workspace knowledge graph and is where almost every business task should start, because it answers who the customer is and how this company writes before you spend a credit guessing. `records` searches the CRM. `web` searches the public internet and costs credits. `capabilities` searches the full catalogue and returns a short-lived capability_ref you then pass to ds_api; this is also how a remote client discovers what exists without reading our filesystem. `skills` lists the procedures that exist, one line each, and you then read the one you want with ds_read on its skill:// address. Search once with a specific query rather than three times with vague ones.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Which corpus to search. This tool uses `scope`, not `action` (every other ds_* tool uses action). One of: context, records, web, capabilities, skills.

fields.name: query
fields.description: Text to search for under context/records/capabilities/skills. Under web it is NOT free-text search: it must be one https:// URL to fetch. Ignored when address (context walk) or ids (records resolve) is set.

fields.name: object
fields.description: records scope only: the CRM object key, e.g. person, company, deal. Never contact.

fields.name: domain
fields.description: capabilities scope only: filter catalogue results to one domain.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: capabilities scope only: filter catalogue results to one kind.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: Max results to return. Defaults to 25.

fields.name: include_schema
fields.description: capabilities scope only. Controls how many leading candidates (by rank, independent of limit) carry input_schema (field name/type/required/description/enum per argument), action_policy (mutation consequence and side-effect class) and cost_policy, so the caller does not have to redeem a capability_ref through ds_api just to see the argument contract before its first call. Every candidate always carries a capability_ref regardless of this setting. Omitted (the default): the first 3 candidates carry the contract. true: widens that to the first 5. false: no candidate carries the contract, for a caller that wants the compact card only.

fields.name: address
fields.description: context scope only: a context:// document address (not a folder) returned by a previous search or read. With address set, this call walks the graph from that node instead of text-searching; query is ignored. Required when walk is set.

fields.name: walk
fields.description: context scope only, requires address. graph: linked neighborhood of the node (also the default when address is set without walk). backlinks: what links to the node.

fields.name: ids
fields.description: records scope only: a batch of record ids to resolve to their display entities (records.references_resolve) instead of a text search. When set, query is ignored. Maximum 100 ids per call.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: Required for scope=web (leaves the workspace and costs credits). Optional elsewhere. One user-facing sentence on what this call is for. Never a security input.

fields.name: max_credits
fields.description: Required for scope=web: a positive credit ceiling for this fetch. research.urls_fetch has no fixed price, so the gateway cannot bound its cost without one. Ignored elsewhere (those scopes are free reads).

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates search shape and policy only. dry_run may read real data but cannot create an effect. live performs the requested search.

tools.name: ds_records
tools.description: The CRM. Read, create and update people, companies, deals and any custom object. The noun is person, never contact. Read a record before changing it and preserve fields a human authored. create requires a TOP-LEVEL display_name (example: display_name="Acme Corp"), not only a name buried in values. get/history/memberships/update/note need a real record id from a prior list or search; do not pass null. `merge` is not casually reversible: it collapses two records and the undo is a separate unmerge that cannot always restore what was lost, so show what will be merged before doing it. `erase` is permanent and exists for privacy requests; `archive` (deals only today) is recoverable and is the one to reach for otherwise. Also owns follow-up tasks: work a human will do later, not a cadence the system runs on its own, which belongs to a sequence or workflow instead. And bulk file transfer in and out of the CRM: `import` for a file of records mapped onto real fields, `export` for a saved view sent out as a file.

fields.name: action
fields.description: CRM verb. Includes generic record/task/import/export actions plus contact_list, contact_get, contact_save, contact_archive, contact_enrich, and compiled_record.

fields.name: object
fields.description: The CRM object key, e.g. person, company, deal. Never contact. Required for create and for list of a typed object; get/update/erase/archive/history/memberships use id instead (set object: deal to reach deal capabilities). archive today only reaches a deal.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Required for get, history, memberships, update, note, list_add, list_remove, archive, erase, and for single-task task_list/task_update/task_transition. A real CRM record id (or task id for task_*), formatted as a UUID. Never null and never a placeholder. If you do not already have one, call ds_records with action=list and object=person (or the relevant object) first, then use an id from that result. memberships/get/history without a known id: list first.

fields.name: winner_id
fields.description: merge only: the record that survives, a UUID. Required with loser_id.

fields.name: loser_id
fields.description: merge only: the record collapsed into winner_id, a UUID. Required with winner_id.

fields.name: snapshot_id
fields.description: unmerge only: required. The merge snapshot to reverse, a UUID.

fields.name: list_id
fields.description: list_add/list_remove only: required. The CRM list (table) id, a UUID.

fields.name: display_name
fields.description: create: REQUIRED top-level display name for the new record (or deal name). Example: display_name="P-C Harness Contact". Put it at the TOP LEVEL of the call, not only inside values. If you also pass values, you may still set values.email and other fields there; the human-readable name itself is display_name. task_create: REQUIRED task title (same top-level field).

fields.name: updates
fields.description: update: required. Exactly one field for a non-deal object. Deal update/move: field patch, or to_stage_id (+ expected_version) when capability_id is deals.move. task_update: one or more of title/description/priority/due_at/queue_id, or exactly assignee_user_id to reassign.

fields.name: values
fields.description: create only: optional initial field map for the new record (email, tags, notes, etc.). Do not put the record name only here: the top-level display_name field is required for create. If display_name is omitted, the facade will accept values.display_name, values.name, or values.full_name as a fallback, but prefer top-level display_name.

fields.name: note
fields.description: note action only: required. Markdown body of the note to append.

fields.name: confirm
fields.description: merge: omit or false previews both records without merging; true performs the merge. erase: required true (permanent).

fields.name: query
fields.description: list only: optional text filter (mapped to capability q).

fields.name: limit
fields.description: list/task_list/history/import_status: page size. Defaults vary by capability (often 50).

fields.name: offset
fields.description: list only: skip this many rows (people/company/generic list).

fields.name: cursor
fields.description: list (deals)/task_list: the string cursor from a previous page. history: the cursor object from a previous page. Always pass back the value you were given verbatim, never construct one.

fields.name: task_ids
fields.description: task_transition only: batch the same transition across several tasks instead of one. When set, id is not required. Maximum 200 task ids per call.

fields.name: transition
fields.description: task_transition only: required. Which lifecycle move to make.

fields.name: count
fields.description: task_list only: when true, return a total (tasks.count) instead of a page of tasks.

fields.name: job_id
fields.description: import/import_status/export/export_status: the transfer job to read or control. Required for status polls and for control/rows_stage/errors_list branches.

fields.name: capability_id
fields.description: Which canonical capability this call reaches, for an action that can reach more than one. Required for import/import_status/export/export_status. Optional elsewhere: history defaults to records.history_get (pass records.buyer_brief_get or records.wiki_get for the other two), memberships defaults to records.memberships_get (pass records.lists_get for named CRM lists), update on a deal defaults to deals.update (pass deals.move with to_stage_id/expected_version to change stage), and erase defaults to records.erase (pass records.value_retire with value_id to retire one field instead).

fields.name: value_id
fields.description: erase with capability_id records.value_retire only: required. The field value id to retire (not the whole record).

fields.name: extra
fields.description: Capability-specific fields this facade does not name individually, e.g. deal pipeline_id/view_id, a task's description/priority/due_at/assignee_user_id/queue_id/links, or the import/export payload fields (object_definition_id, base64, mapping, saved_view_id, projection, rows, action, and so on).

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: Required by dispatch for every mutating action (create, update, note, list_add, list_remove, merge, unmerge, erase, task_*, import, export). One user-facing sentence. Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: dry_run previews without effect; only honoured when the resolved capability declares dry_run_supported. Otherwise expect preview_unsupported and use live after confirming the intended change. merge already previews for free when confirm is omitted; mode is independent of that.

tools.name: ds_workbook
tools.description: Build and enrich a list of people or companies, and define the outreach sequence they get enrolled into. This is the tool with the most ways to waste money, so load the workbook skill before using it beyond a simple read. In short: read the existing columns by their exact names, preview a source on a handful of rows BEFORE creating anything, build one column at a time, set run conditions as a separate call after the column exists, and treat the first real run as a sample to review rather than a finished deliverable. Every row is credits already spent, so archive rather than delete. To write a multi-step outreach sequence (e.g. a 3-step LinkedIn + email cadence): validate the definition, bind it to get a version, publish that version, then enroll rows into it.

fields.name: action
fields.description: Workbook verb. 27 values including the free cost-guards preview and preview_cost (call those before add_column/run/run_all). One of: get, list, list_columns, read_cells, inspect_cell, preview, preview_cost, resolve_facets, audit, create, update, duplicate, archive, add_column, edit_column, remove_column, reorder_columns, set_run_condition, attach_source, detach_source, run, run_all, cancel_run, retry_run, send_rows, enroll, transfer.

fields.name: capability_id
fields.description: Which canonical capability this action compiles to. Always required, even when the action has only one legal value: list_columns pass columns.list, preview_cost pass table_runs.preview_cost, resolve_facets pass linkedin.search_parameters_list, add_column pass columns.add, edit_column pass columns.update, remove_column pass columns.archive, reorder_columns pass worksheets.reorder, set_run_condition pass columns.update, detach_source pass table_sources.detach, cancel_run pass table_runs.cancel. For get, list, read_cells, inspect_cell, preview, audit, create, update, duplicate, archive, attach_source, run, run_all, retry_run, send_rows, enroll, transfer, the action can reach more than one capability, so name the one you mean.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Exact input fields for the resolved capability (table_id/workbook_id/worksheet_id, column_id, filters, source config, etc.). Every field below is declared by at least one reachable capability; each field's own description names which capability requires it. Use list_columns for exact column names, then ds_search scope=capabilities or the workbook skill for the per-capability shape. preview/preview_cost params are samples and cost estimates only; they do not create columns.

fields.name: expected_updated_at
fields.description: edit_column only, required with expected_binding_revision. Read the column immediately before editing it and pass back its current updated_at.

fields.name: expected_binding_revision
fields.description: edit_column only, required with expected_updated_at. Read the column immediately before editing it and pass back its current binding_revision. Binding revisions auto-increment on any binding change, so a stale value is rejected rather than silently applied.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: Required by dispatch for every mutating action (create through transfer). Optional for reads including preview and preview_cost. One user-facing sentence. Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates the selected request and policy without reads, providers, credits, or effects. dry_run previews without effect; only honoured when the resolved capability declares dry_run_supported. Otherwise expect preview_unsupported and use live (the default) after confirming the intended change. Prefer preview/preview_cost before a costly run/run_all regardless of mode.

fields.name: max_credits
fields.description: Optional credit ceiling for this call. Pair with preview_cost before run/run_all.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key for safe retries of a mutating call.

tools.name: ds_publish
tools.description: The post lifecycle. A post is not a boolean: it moves draft, submit_review, approve, schedule, publish, and each transition is a separate act. Content approval moves an artifact through its lifecycle; it is NOT authorization to make something public, which is a different decision. Draft and iterate in chat before creating the artifact. Publishing is outward-facing and returns a receipt with the provider and external id, not a diff.

fields.name: action
fields.description: Lifecycle step: get, list, draft, update, submit_review, approve, schedule, unschedule, post, republish, rollback, archive. approve is not post.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Exact input fields for the selected capability_id. Shapes differ per capability (for example content.delivery_publish requires delivery_id; content.artifact_create requires content, channels, account_ids). Every field below is declared by at least one reachable capability; each field's own description names which capability requires it. Fetch the capability contract first via ds_search scope=capabilities to confirm the exact set for the capability_id you selected; do not invent field names outside this list.

fields.name: capability_id
fields.description: Canonical capability this action compiles to. Always required. For unschedule pass content.unschedule, for rollback pass content.version_rollback, for archive pass content.artifact_archive. For get, list, draft, update, submit_review, approve, schedule, post, republish the action can reach more than one capability, so name the one you mean; a wrong-but-valid selection is refused with the allowed ids listed in repair.expected. Search capabilities before inventing an id.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: One user-facing sentence on what this call is for. Required by dispatch for every mutating action (draft through archive). Omit only for pure reads (get, list). Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates the selected capability and policy without reads, providers, credits, or effects. dry_run may read but cannot create an external effect. live executes.

fields.name: max_credits
fields.description: Optional credit ceiling for this call. Omit to use the gateway default. Never a security input.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key for a deliberate retry of the same mutation. Omit for a first call; dispatch derives a stable key from the resolved request so a retry collapses onto its predecessor. Supply your own only when two deliberately identical mutations must both run.

tools.name: ds_plan
tools.description: Content strategy and the weekly plan. This is the calendar of what will be written, which is a different job from writing it: plan here, write with ds_publish. Read the strategy overview and the archetype benchmarks before suggesting anything, so suggestions are anchored to what this workspace is actually trying to do. Materialize a plan item into an artifact before transitioning it.

fields.name: action
fields.description: Plan step: overview, benchmarks, calendar, suggest, update_strategy, materialize, item_create, item_update, item_transition. Materialize before item_transition when the item must become a real artifact first.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Exact input fields for the selected capability_id. Shapes differ per capability (for example materialize takes item_id; strategy reads often take social_sender_profile_id). Every field below is declared by at least one reachable capability; each field's own description names which capability requires it. Fetch the capability contract first via ds_search scope=capabilities; do not invent field names outside this list.

fields.name: capability_id
fields.description: Canonical capability this action compiles to. Always required. For materialize pass social.strategy_weekly_post_materialize, for item_create pass social.weekly_plan_item_create, for item_update pass social.weekly_plan_item_update. For overview, benchmarks, calendar, suggest, update_strategy, item_transition the action can reach more than one capability, so name the one you mean; a wrong-but-valid selection is refused with the allowed ids listed in repair.expected. Search capabilities before inventing an id.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: One user-facing sentence on what this call is for. Required by dispatch for every mutating action (suggest, update_strategy, materialize, item_create, item_update, item_transition). Omit only for pure reads (overview, benchmarks, calendar). Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates the selected request and policy without reads, providers, credits, or effects. dry_run previews without effect only when the selected capability declares dry_run_supported. Otherwise expect preview_unsupported and use live after confirming the intended change.

fields.name: max_credits
fields.description: Optional credit ceiling for this call. Omit to use the gateway default. Never a security input.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key for a deliberate retry of the same mutation. Omit for a first call; dispatch derives a stable key from the resolved request so a retry collapses onto its predecessor. Supply your own only when two deliberately identical mutations must both run.

tools.name: ds_analytics
tools.description: Reporting on what already happened: post performance, audience, sequence results and workspace usage. Read the metric definitions before querying, because a metric that sounds obvious here often is not. `refresh` costs credits and pulls from providers, so do not refresh reflexively before every read; the stored numbers carry the timestamp they were collected at and you should quote it.

fields.name: action
fields.description: Analytics step: post, audience, query, sequences, workflows, usage, refresh. refresh costs credits and pulls from providers; prefer stored numbers with their collected_at first.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Exact input fields for the selected capability_id. Shapes differ per capability (for example social.post_analytics requires platform, account_id, provider_post_id; usage.status_get takes no fields). Every field below is declared by at least one reachable capability; each field's own description names which capability requires it. Fetch the capability contract first via ds_search scope=capabilities; do not invent field names outside this list.

fields.name: capability_id
fields.description: Canonical capability this action compiles to. Always required. For audience pass social.audience_analytics. For post, query, sequences, workflows, usage, refresh the action can reach more than one capability, so name the one you mean; a wrong-but-valid selection is refused with the allowed ids listed in repair.expected. Search capabilities before inventing an id.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: One user-facing sentence on what this call is for. Required by dispatch for mutating actions (refresh). Omit for pure reads. Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates the selected request and policy without reads, providers, credits, or effects. dry_run previews without effect only when the selected capability declares dry_run_supported. Otherwise expect preview_unsupported and use live.

fields.name: max_credits
fields.description: Optional credit ceiling for this call. Relevant for refresh and other metered pulls. Omit to use the gateway default. Never a security input.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key for a deliberate retry of the same mutation (refresh). Omit for a first call; dispatch derives a stable key from the resolved request so a retry collapses onto its predecessor. Supply your own only when two deliberately identical mutations must both run.

tools.name: ds_engage
tools.description: The inbox and the reply surface: notifications, engagement opportunities and comments. A comment is public the moment it posts, so draft it, show it, and only then publish. Notification pulls are paged and cost credits, so pull once and work through what came back rather than pulling repeatedly.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Capability input fields under their exact catalogue names. notifications: social.linkedin_notifications_list takes action?, limit?, offset?; social.linkedin_post_notifications_list takes delivery_id (uuid); social.linkedin_notification_subscriptions_list takes {}. opportunities: engagement.opportunities.list takes source_domain?, status? (new|engaged|skipped|archived|all), limit?, offset?; engagement.opportunities.counts takes {}; engagement.people_engaged_n_times takes min_count (required int), window_days?, kinds?, account_ids?, cursor?. conversations: outreach.dm_conversations_list takes source?, sort?, limit?, search?; outreach.dm_conversation_get takes conversation_urn; outreach.dm_conversation_by_contact_get takes contact_id (uuid). pull: account_id (uuid, required), since? (datetime). subscribe and unsubscribe: account_id (uuid). status_set: engagement.opportunities.status_set takes opportunity_id (uuid), expected_updated_at (datetime), status (engaged|skipped|archived); outreach.dm_conversation_status_update takes conversation_urn, status; outreach.dm_conversation_read takes conversation_urn. comment: social.comment_publish takes account_id (uuid), target_post_urn, body, consequence set to the literal public_comment; social.reddit_comment_publish takes account_id (uuid), parent_thing_id, body, consequence set to the literal public_comment. reply: conversation_urn, client_request_id (uuid, required), body?. Do not invent synonyms: text is not body, conversation_id is not conversation_urn, opportunity_id alone is not enough for comment.

fields.name: capability_id
fields.description: Always required, even when the action has only one legal value. notifications: social.linkedin_notifications_list | social.linkedin_post_notifications_list | social.linkedin_notification_subscriptions_list. opportunities: engagement.opportunities.list | engagement.opportunities.counts | engagement.people_engaged_n_times. conversations: outreach.dm_conversations_list | outreach.dm_conversation_get | outreach.dm_conversation_by_contact_get. status_set: engagement.opportunities.status_set | outreach.dm_conversation_status_update | outreach.dm_conversation_read. comment: social.comment_publish | social.reddit_comment_publish. pull pass social.linkedin_notifications_pull, subscribe pass social.linkedin_notifications_subscribe, unsubscribe pass social.linkedin_notifications_unsubscribe, reply pass outreach.dm_message_send.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: Required for write actions (pull, subscribe, unsubscribe, status_set, comment, reply): one user-facing sentence on what this call is for. Optional for pure read actions (notifications, opportunities, conversations).

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates the selected request and policy without reads, providers, credits, or effects. live executes. dry_run is refused for every capability this tool reaches today (none declare dry_run_supported). For comment and reply, put the exact body in front of the user before mode: live; do not call dry_run expecting a preview.

fields.name: max_credits
fields.description: Optional credit ceiling for this call. Omit to use the gateway default. Never a security input.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional idempotency key for a deliberate retry of the same mutation. Omit for a first call; dispatch derives a stable key from the resolved request so a retry collapses onto its predecessor. Supply your own only when two deliberately identical mutations must both run.

tools.name: ds_api
tools.description: The escape hatch to any capability that does not have a named tool. Two stage by design: call ds_search scope=capabilities first to get a capability_ref, then execute against that ref. The ref binds the capability id, its schema version, the policy version, the principal and an expiry, so the schema cannot drift between when you read it and when you call it. This path is governed identically to every named tool: a publish reached through ds_api gets exactly what ds_publish gets. Prefer a named tool when one exists, because it carries the procedure and the traps.

fields.name: action
fields.description: Always run. The only action this tool declares.

fields.name: capability_ref
fields.description: Minted by ds_search scope=capabilities (never invent one, never pass a raw capability id). Short lived, principal-bound and workspace-bound. On expiry, mismatch or schema drift, search again.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Input fields of the RESOLVED capability under its exact catalogue names. The capability_ref seals the schema version; required keys are those the catalogue declared when the ref was minted. Prefer a named tool when one exists, because named tools carry the procedure and the traps.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: One user-facing sentence on what this call is trying to obtain. Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates the selected request and policy without reads, providers, credits, or effects. live executes. dry_run is refused unless the RESOLVED capability declares dry_run_supported; most catalogue entries do not. This tool declares itself mutating as a conservative ceiling at authoring time; the dispatcher lowers the effect class to the resolved capability real class (a read stays reversible).

fields.name: max_credits
fields.description: Optional credit ceiling for this one call.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional caller-supplied idempotency key. When omitted on a mutation, the dispatcher derives one from the resolved request.

tools.name: ds_ask
tools.description: Ask the user something, or open a canvas. Ask only when the answer materially changes what you build AND you cannot derive it from the request, the context graph, the current surface or a live contract. A required parameter you can derive is not a missing answer. Never ask a question the work itself would answer, never ask the user to diagnose a failed tool call, and never ask permission to do the thing they already asked for. One consolidated popup carrying every remaining question, after the partial work exists. After it opens, stop: the answer resumes a new turn from durable state.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: One user-facing sentence on what this call is trying to obtain. Never a security input.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: smoke_test validates this request only and opens no popup or canvas. dry_run is non-effecting validation for this tool. live opens the requested interaction.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: The chat session whose durable turn this question belongs to. Required for question.

fields.name: checkpoint_kind
fields.description: Defaults to consequence. intake is the opening checkpoint a turn opens for itself. For consequence, the server assigns every questions[].concept_id to approval_consequence. For external_prerequisite, it assigns every questions[].concept_id to external_prerequisite. Do not supply either value yourself.

fields.name: questions
fields.description: question: REQUIRED. One or more questions to put to the user in a single checkpoint. Maximum 13 questions per call, one per intake concept; split genuinely distinct checkpoints into separate calls instead of exceeding it.

fields.name: artifact_id
fields.description: An id a live call returned. A synthesized id is refused.
